title: Pet-Friendly Interiors That Don't Look Like a Kennel
description: How to design a home that survives claws, fur and mud without giving up on style. Fabric picks, flooring that lasts and colors that hide shedding.
excerpt: You don't have to choose between a good-looking apartment and a happy dog. You just have to pick the right materials the first time.
content:
A boucle sofa and a cat is a combination you get to try exactly once. After that you're just counting pulled loops. The good news: a home with animals can look great — you just decide differently.

## Materials that actually survive

For upholstery you want a tight weave: microfiber, performance outdoor fabric, or real leather. Claws slide off because there's nothing to hook into. Boucle, chenille, linen and anything with a visible loop is out.

On the floor, luxury vinyl or tile beats soft wood. Oak at hardness 3 handles more than pine. And for rugs, use carpet tiles — when one gets ruined you replace one square, not the whole rug.

## Plan for fur and smell up front

Pick your color around the animal, not the other way round. A black sofa with a white dog is a daily fight. Mid-grey, heathered or patterned fabric hides about 80% of what you'd otherwise vacuum every day.

Washable textiles are the gold standard. Removable covers, machine-washable throws, runners you can toss in at 40°C. Anything you can't wash smells within a year.

## Test it before you buy

The expensive mistake is buying a sofa you hate a month later. Photograph the room and drop it into [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io) — the AI shows you how the space looks with a darker fabric, a different rug, or rearranged furniture. Five options in ten minutes, then you order.

And when you're sending apartment photos to an agent or a listing, [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) compresses them without killing the quality, right in your browser.
